§11.1.3 Multiple Charts and Reference Ink

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

charts-multiple-charts-and-reference-ink · charts structure

✅ Normative

Each chart or panel on a page MUST get its own chart table, and every panel MUST be covered (see Cover Every Data Point§11.1.1). Reference ink — labeled averages, trend lines, shaded bands, event callouts — draws no data points and MUST NOT be rendered as data: it gets no row, no column and no value in any chart table. Its printed text MUST still be kept.

Several charts on one page

Every chart and every panel of a multi-panel figure is its own chart table, in reading order, with its printed title or panel heading in <caption>. The same one-row-per-position, one-column-per-series coverage applies to each. Where charts share a label set, each table's caption tells them apart (see Labels§11.1.2).

A caption shared by several panels MUST appear once: first inside the first panel's table when read before the group, or last inside the last panel's table when read after the group. A shared caption and that panel's own title are kept in printed order within the same <caption>.

Ink printed once for several panels — a shared axis title, a single legend serving every panel — MUST NOT be lost:

  • a shared legend names the series of every panel it serves, so each panel's table carries those series names as its column headers;
  • a shared axis title is printed text of the figure and is kept once, as text.

Reference ink is not data

Reference ink Why it is not data
A labeled average or trend line (10-year average, a line fitted through a scatter) it summarises the data points; it is not one of them
A shaded band or background region it marks a span of the axis, not a value
An event callout naming a year (1976: Tangshan Earthquake, China — see Log Scale Charts§11.2.6) it comments on a point; its value is the point's own

A chart table that gains a column for a trend line, or a row for a shaded band, contains values the chart never drew as data — invented content (see Never Drop, Never Invent§2.2). The printed labels of reference ink are text on the page, kept as text, after the table in reading order — see the chart table's layout in Cover Every Data Point§11.1.1.

✅ Sample — RenewablesDeploymentTracker2024_p13

Six titled panels — five bar panels (World, China, European Union, United States, India) over the same five years, and one horizontal panel (Avoided emissions) over regions — every bar printing its value: 30 values in six tables. Each single-series panel is headed by its value-axis title (GW, Mt CO₂). China appears both as a panel and as a row of the avoided-emissions panel; each table's title keeps them apart. The bar values are printed in bold. The running header and tab label are elided.

✅ Sample — two panels sharing a legend and an axis

Two bar panels stacked vertically, each with its own underlined period caption (1960–1973, 1973–1980), over one rotated axis title on the far left and one legend that serves both. Each panel is its own table, and both tables carry the three legend series as their headers: read alone, the lower panel's bars are unnamed. The axis title, printed once, is kept once. Every bar prints its value; the printed minus signs are written -. The lower panel runs negative, bars descending below a zero line that crosses the panel. In the lower panel, the value label under Marolia's second bar is covered by the bar itself and that bar is drawn both above and below the zero line, so the Marolia row is elided. The running header is elided.

✅ Sample — sixteen small panels under two captions

Figure 3a and Figure 3b hold eight stacked-bar panels each, every panel headed by its deposition type and its element's flux title, each drawing ten stacks of four fill colours. No panel prints a site name, a tick value or a legend, so no bar can be located or calibrated: the panels carry no chart table, and the output keeps their printed headings and titles, in reading order. Figure 3b and the text below it are elided.

✅ Sample — recession bands behind four lines


Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Monthly Labor Review, February 2003, Chart 5 and Table 4 (public domain)

Four line styles, each named by a direct label with a leader line, over 33 years (1970–2002, the axis labeling every second year as 1970, 72, 74 …) and five grey vertical bands that the note says are recessions. The four named series are the table's columns; the bands are reference ink and add nothing to it, while the note that explains them is kept. No value is printed, so every cell is an estimate against the 2-point grid. Only the first two labeled years are shown; the table continues through 02, and the table sharing the page is elided.
